description: ODC (EDIT coverage over STRUCTURE): touch a COMPOSITE TYPE that this job did not create, and see what happens to whoever uses it as a parameter type and as an output type. The base is job:structure-nested, that is, the four nested structures (WfCovGeoPoint, WfCovAddress, WfCovCoverageItem, WfCovPolicyQuote) and the public server action WfCovQuote_Build already exist when the first op runs - there is no spec op here on purpose, because creating and editing in the same job proves no maintenance at all. The target is the inherited WfCovAddress, chosen because it is the only one that plays the THREE roles at the same time: type of the input Address, type of the nested attribute WfCovPolicyQuote.Address (which in turn is the type of the output Quote) and owner of an attribute read by an expression (Quote.Address.Zone). The four changes are all on top of state that the OTHER job left written: add the attribute WfCountry to a structure that already had its 4 attributes, swap the DataType of Postcode (Text -> Integer) in an attribute that already existed, rename the attribute Zone to District WITH an inherited expression reading it, and rename the structure itself to WfCovLocation with three real consumers connected. Outside the job that created them there are no aliases: the structures are cited by 'IStructure:Name', the attributes by the path 'IStructure:Name/Attribute' and the parameters of the inherited action by 'IServerAction:WfCovQuote_Build/Address'. The central lesson is in the difference between the last two changes: renaming the ATTRIBUTE rewrites by itself the expression that reads it (Quote.Address.Zone becomes Quote.Address.District), but renaming the TYPE touches no expression at all - because no expression cites the name of the type, they cite the name of the PARAMETER (Address) and of the attribute. Whoever holds the type holds it by KEY: the input Address, the output Quote and the nested attribute come out of the rename with the same DataType and without a single manual correction; what is left behind is the Description of the structure, written here on purpose citing WfCovAddress.Zone, two names that at the end of the job no longer exist. The last pair of ops is something else: a write on a NAMED TOP-LEVEL ELEMENT (the inherited server action), which the data contract started to watch besides the entities - the Description of the consumer does not follow anything and only a hand puts it telling the truth about the new contract.

ops.name: WfCovAddress
ops._why: (0) starting point: the structure ALREADY exists before the first op of this job. It comes from the base job:structure-nested, not from a spec here. The find also returns the 'WfCovAddress Record' that the platform generated with it - the IAnonymousStructure that is the record type the parameters use

(1) BEFORE, the structure: Attributes 4, Public True (in ODC vocabulary, shareable) and the Description written by the other job. It is public because the action that receives it is public, and in ODC a shareable action only exposes shareable types
(2) BEFORE, the tree: the 4 attributes in birth order (Street, Postcode, Zone, Geo), the last of them already composite. This is the photograph that the dump (15) is compared with
(3) BEFORE, the attribute that is going to change type: DataType Text, IndexInParent 1, empty Length, empty Description. Note that the Label is NOT empty: the platform always derives it from the name

(4) BEFORE, the attribute that is going to be renamed: Referrers counts who holds it. It is the only attribute of this structure that an inherited expression reads by the full path (Quote.Address.Zone), and that is why I chose it - renaming an attribute that nobody reads proves no propagation at all

(5) BEFORE, the PARAMETER-CONSUMER: the input Address of the inherited action, with DataType pointing to the key of WfCovAddress. Keep this key: in the get (13e) it has to be the same, after the structure has changed its name

(6) BEFORE, the OUTPUT-CONSUMER: the output of the action is of type WfCovPolicyQuote, which is not the target of this job. It only touches WfCovAddress on the inside, through the nested attribute of the get (7) - so it is the proof that the edit reaches whoever never cites the edited type

(7) BEFORE, the NESTING-CONSUMER: the attribute Address of the top structure has as DataType the same key as the input of the get (5). A composite type used as a field of another is a consumer like the others, only inside the data model

(8) BEFORE, who holds the structure: count 10, real 10 - the attribute of the top structure, the input of the action, the IAttribute of the anonymous record and seven expressions. None of those expressions cites the name 'WfCovAddress': they cite Address (the parameter) and Quote.Address (the attribute). Keep that for the rename of the type, further down
(9) BEFORE, the text in writing: the inherited expressions say 'Holder + " - " + Quote.Address.Zone' and 'Address.Geo.Latitude > 26.0'. It is against this dump that the dumps (12d) and (13h) are read

ops.value: Morada de uma apolice. O distrito vive em WfCovAddress.Zone.
ops._why: author text written NOW, before the two renames, and on purpose citing the TWO names that are going to disappear. It is not decoration: it is the trap set by the hands of this job, so that the get (12e) and the get (13c) show that Description is text and not a reference - no rename touches it

ops.name: WfCountry
ops._why: (10a) CHANGE 1 - add an attribute to the INHERITED structure. The parent is not an $alias: aliases are local to the job that declares them, and the one that declared this structure was another job. Outside it the stable reference is 'IStructure:WfCovAddress'. The Wf prefix is because the attribute is NEW; those that already existed keep the convention of the structure

ops.value: Codigo do pais em ISO 3166-1 alfa-2. Acrescentado por structure-lifecycle.json, DEPOIS de a structure existir e de ja haver quem a use como tipo.

ops._why: (10b) AFTER: the new attribute enters at the END of the sequence (IndexInParent 4, after Geo) and not in the middle. The alias $country only exists because THIS job created it - it is the difference between what is inherited and what is added

(10c) AFTER, the tree: 5 attributes where the dump (2) showed 4, and the 4 inherited in the same order. THE LESSON: the input Address of the action and the output Quote have just changed SHAPE without a single op touching them - whoever holds a composite type by contract inherits the contract that the type has at the moment, and a new field reaches everyone at once

(11a) CHANGE 2 - swap the DataType of an attribute that ALREADY EXISTED. I chose Postcode and not Zone or Geo on purpose: Postcode is the only attribute of this structure that NO inherited expression reads. Swapping the type under a live expression is another experiment, and a negative one - the Verify would fall into ExpressionUnexpectedExpresssionType because 'Holder + " - " + Quote.Address.Zone' requires Text. The rename rewrites text; the type swap rewrites nothing, it only changes what the old expression now requires

(11b) AFTER: compare with the get (3). The DataType CHANGED (Text -> Integer); the IndexInParent 1, the Name, the IsMandatory and the key REMAINED - the attribute did not change place or identity, only type. And because it is the SAME key, the (11c) still has something to read

(11c) AFTER, the parameter-consumer: strictly equal to the get (5), the same DataType key. The parameter does not know that a field of its type has changed type, and that is why the swap is dangerous: it does not show up anywhere on the consumer's side, only when the Verify of whatever expression ends up touching it runs
(12a) BEFORE the rename: who reads the attribute. The expression of the Assign SetHeader is here, and it is the one that the rename has to rewrite by itself

ops.name: District
ops._why: (12b) CHANGE 3 - rename an INHERITED attribute with a real consumer connected. It is a rename, not a creation: so it follows the convention of the structure and does NOT take the Wf prefix of the new elements. Read consumers and expressionsRewritten, but do not deliver based on them - the proof is in the dump (12d)

(12c) AFTER: the path is now '/District' (the old one stopped resolving), the key is the same as in the get (4) and the Label followed, because it was derived from the name and nobody had fixed it by hand. A Label written by 'set' would have stayed with the old text, like that of WfCovProject in edit-inherited-data.json

(12d) THE CENTRAL PROOF of this change: the inherited expression already says 'Holder + " - " + Quote.Address.District' without a single manual correction. The rewritten segment is only the LAST one - 'Quote' is still the output and 'Address' is still the nested attribute, because neither of the two was renamed. Compare word by word with the dump (9)

(12e) READ BACK WHAT DID NOT FOLLOW: the Description still says 'o distrito vive em WfCovAddress.Zone', an attribute that no longer exists. Description is the author's text, not a binding: only a hand corrects it

ops.name: WfCovLocation
ops._why: (13a) CHANGE 4 - rename the inherited STRUCTURE itself, with three real consumers connected (input, nested attribute and anonymous record) and seven expressions nearby. The name was wrong: it does not hold only an address, it holds the location, with the geographic point inside

ops.name: WfCovAddress
ops._why: (13b) EMPTY list: the inherited name disappeared from the module. Compare with the find (0), which returned TWO objects with this name - the IStructure and the IAttribute of the anonymous record 'WfCovAddress Record'. Both followed the rename, and none was left behind. The find is the right read for this question: the counter of the rename says how many consumers there were, not whether the old name still exists somewhere
(13c) AFTER: new Name, SAME key as the get (1), Attributes 5 and the Description still citing WfCovAddress.Zone - the two old names, together, in a text that survived two renames

(13d) the consumers of the get (8), with the SAME keys and the same count: none broke and none was born. What changed in text was the path of the anonymous record, which became 'WfCovLocation Record' because its name is derived from the name of the type

(13e) AFTER, the parameter-consumer: the DataType is the SAME key as the get (5). The input is still called Address - the name of the parameter is a choice of the author of the action and does not follow the name of the type, just as the node 'Describe' did not follow the rename of the action in refactor-inherited.json
(13f) AFTER, the nesting-consumer: same key as the get (7), and the attribute is still called Address inside WfCovPolicyQuote. Renaming the TYPE does not rename the FIELDS that use it

(13g) AFTER, the output-consumer: identical to the get (6). Renaming WfCovAddress did not touch WfCovPolicyQuote, only what it points to inside - the output of the action kept the type, the name and the key

(13h) THE LESSON that separates this change from the previous one: no expression changed between the dump (12d) and this one. Renaming an ATTRIBUTE rewrites the expressions that read it; renaming the TYPE rewrites nothing, because no expression cites the name of the type - it cites the parameter (Address), the output (Quote) and the attributes. Whoever expects to see 'WfCovLocation' here is looking for a word that was never written

ops.value: Constroi a cotacao. Contrato actualizado por structure-lifecycle.json: o input Address e agora do tipo WfCovLocation, com o campo WfCountry, e o antigo Zone chama-se District.
ops._why: (14a) NAMED TOP-LEVEL ELEMENT: the inherited action is the consumer, and its Description followed neither the rename of the type nor that of the attribute - it was necessary to come here and write it by hand. It is also the write with which this job exercises the extended data contract: besides entities and structures, it started to watch properties written on named top-level elements, and a write that did not settle would fail the job with 'Data property mismatch' even with a clean Verify

(14b) READ BACK the top-level write: the Description is this job's, word by word, and the action still exposes 3 inputs and 1 output. Note the pair Public True / Shareable True: it is the SAME value with the two names, that of the API and that of the ODC product, and it is what requires WfCovLocation to remain public after all these changes. This read is the same check that the data contract does by itself at the end - the difference is that the contract does not depend on someone remembering to write it

(15) The final tree, to be put next to the dump (2): the same object, with another name, 5 attributes instead of 4, WfCountry at the end and not in the middle, Postcode in the same place with another type and Zone with the name District. Four changes, zero rebuilds: the key is the same as in the first get

(16) WHAT REMAINED: the neighboring structure, from the same base and one level below, intact - same name, same Description, same 2 attributes. It is the counter-proof that this job edited what it chose and did not rebuild the model underneath; if there were a spec here, this read would be worthless
